text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared central repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, this happens many times a day. The core of CI is the automated build process. Every time new code is pushed, the system automatically compiles the entire project. Immediately after, a series of automated tests are run. This approach is highly effective at catching issues early, often within minutes of a change being made. If a test fails, the team is alerted right away, preventing small problems from becoming major bugs later. All these steps are orchestrated through CI pipelines, which guide the code from the initial commit through testing and beyond, ensuring the software remains stable.
